questionText:
For positive real numbers $S$ and $K$, the function $H_K(S)$ is defined as: $H_K(S) = \max(S - K, 0)$. The max function is defined as:

$$\max(a, b) = \begin{cases} a, & \text{when } a > b \\ b, & \text{when } a \le b \end{cases}$$

The graph below shows the plot of a function $N(S)$ versus $S$.

$N(S)$ can be expressed as ________.
explanation:
Step 1: Definition of the base function $H_K(S)$
For $H_K(S) = \max(S - K, 0)$:
• $H_K(S) = 0$ for $S \le K$
• $H_K(S) = S - K$ for $S > K$

Step 2: Analyze Option (A): $N(S) = H_{10}(S) - H_{20}(S)$ across different intervals
• Interval 1: $S \le 10$
$H_{10}(S) = 0$ and $H_{20}(S) = 0 \implies N(S) = 0 - 0 = 0$.

• Interval 2: $10 < S \le 20$
$H_{10}(S) = S - 10$ and $H_{20}(S) = 0 \implies N(S) = (S - 10) - 0 = S - 10$.
At $S = 20$, $N(20) = 20 - 10 = 10$, which creates a line rising from $(10, 0)$ to $(20, 10)$.

• Interval 3: $S > 20$
$H_{10}(S) = S - 10$ and $H_{20}(S) = S - 20 \implies N(S) = (S - 10) - (S - 20) = 10$.
This creates a horizontal line at $N(S) = 10$ for $S > 20$.

Step 3: Conclusion
The piecewise behavior of $H_{10}(S) - H_{20}(S)$ matches the given graph exactly.

Therefore, $N(S) = H_{10}(S) - H_{20}(S)$ (Option A).
